# Piyush Rajput

I'm Piyush, a Computer Science and Engineering student at Karnavati University. I learn by making: 3D learning experiences, conversational AI projects, database applications, and experiments that connect software with the physical world.

## Projects

### Tridix

[Project notes](/projects/tridix/)

**Status:** Built

Physics, beyond the flat page. A browser-based learning experience that brings concepts into three dimensions.

**Purpose:** Physics concepts can be difficult to grasp through written explanations and flat diagrams alone. Tridix was created to make them more visual for students, particularly Class 11 Science learners.

**Technologies / scope:** HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js, Blender

#### Approach

- Built the web experience using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
- Used Blender in the model workflow and Three.js to bring 3D content into the browser.
- Explored AVIF images, lazy loading, and font preloading to improve media delivery.

#### Outcome

A built 3D physics-learning website. The supplied record describes the project as previously unhosted.

#### Documented limits

- A current public deployment and repository URL have not been supplied.
- The exact model inventory and interaction capabilities remain to be documented.
- Historical performance scores are omitted because their project/version attribution needs verification.

### LegalOne

[Project notes](/projects/legalone/)

**Status:** Hackathon project

A conversational starting point for Indian legal information, explored with team Binary Bandits.

**Purpose:** Legal terminology and complex resources can make it difficult to begin finding information about Indian laws. LegalOne explores a more approachable conversational entry point.

**Technologies / scope:** Botpress AI, Conversational AI

#### Approach

- Worked with team Binary Bandits on the OlympAI project.
- Used Botpress AI to develop the chatbot experience around Indian legal information.
- Explored applying conversational AI to a focused information domain.

#### Outcome

Team Binary Bandits cleared Stage 2 of OlympAI.

#### Documented limits

- The precise prototype scope, individual role, and public deployment are not documented in the supplied record.
- This is a legal-information chatbot concept; no legal accuracy guarantee or professional endorsement is claimed.

### Meghdoot AI

[Project notes](/projects/meghdoot-ai/)

**Status:** SIH team project

A flood-detection project explored across an app, web application, and website for Smart India Hackathon.

**Purpose:** Flood-related challenges motivated a team project exploring how digital technology could support detection and disaster-related work.

**Technologies / scope:** App, Web application, Website

#### Approach

- Participated in Smart India Hackathon during the first year of B.Tech.
- Worked with the SIH team on Meghdoot AI, described across an app, web application, and website.
- Presented the project through the college-level selection process.

#### Outcome

Qualified through the college-level round and was among the top 90 teams.

#### Documented limits

- The detection method, model, data sources, technical stack, and individual responsibilities have not been supplied.
- College-level qualification is the documented result; no national finalist or winner status is claimed.

### BRTS Bus Route System

[Project notes](/projects/brts/)

**Status:** Terminal prototype

From command line to interface: working with bus-route information using Python and MySQL.

**Purpose:** This application explores how bus-route information can be handled through a database-backed Python workflow.

**Technologies / scope:** Python, MySQL, Tkinter

#### Approach

- Developed a terminal-based prototype using Python and MySQL.
- Later worked on a Tkinter graphical interface.
- Explored the transition from a command-line workflow toward a desktop application.

#### Outcome

A terminal prototype and subsequent GUI development work.

#### Documented limits

- The exact implemented route features and database schema are not supplied.
- A completed, database-connected Tkinter interface is not confirmed.

### Smart Calendar

[Project notes](/projects/smart-calendar/)

**Status:** Exploring

A physical student calendar concept: dates, tasks, reminders, and a little more connection to everyday life.

**Purpose:** The concept explores making a physical calendar more useful for students by bringing date indicators, tasks, and reminders into one device.

**Technologies / scope:** ESP32 / ESP32-S3, WS2812B LEDs, 20×4 LCD, DS3231 RTC

#### Approach

- Explored an ESP32-based controller with programmable LED calendar indicators.
- Considered an LCD task display, RTC timekeeping, reminder controls, and Wi-Fi connectivity.
- Experimented with circuit configuration, output control, display integration, and power requirements.

#### Outcome

Hardware and circuit exploration in development; a completed working prototype is not confirmed.

#### Documented limits

- Component integration and working features require prototype evidence.
- Google Classroom integration remains a planned feature, not a completed implementation.

### Autonomous Driving Robot

[Project notes](/projects/autonomous-robot/)

**Status:** Architecture exploration

Exploring the bridge from perception to movement, through a proposed two-board autonomous robot architecture.

**Purpose:** The RoboFest Gujarat 5.0 Junior AI Autonomous Driving Bots category prompted a design for lane following, obstacle avoidance, and traffic-signal response.

**Technologies / scope:** Raspberry Pi 3, Raspberry Pi 4, SPI, IR / ultrasonic sensors, L298N

#### Approach

- Proposed separating camera and AI processing on Raspberry Pi 4 from sensor and motor control on Raspberry Pi 3.
- Planned SPI communication between the boards.
- Considered cameras, IR and ultrasonic sensors, an L298N motor driver, and DC geared motors within competition constraints.

#### Outcome

Robot architecture and component planning. No completed autonomous test performance or competition result is confirmed.

#### Documented limits

- A fully assembled robot, implemented perception method, and working board communication are not verified.
- No award, rank, or qualification is claimed.

### Robotics

**Context:** Hardware experience and architecture exploration

Camera input, sensing, control signals, and architecture planning form my current hardware explorations.

- Raspberry Pi 3 & Raspberry Pi 4
- Camera modules / OV5647
- Picamera2 & camera command-line tools
- Camera frame handling
- L298N motor driver
- DC geared motors & four-wheel platforms
- IR line sensors
- US-100 / ultrasonic sensors
- Servo motors
- Buck converters
- LCD modules & buzzers
- GPIO connections & motor-control mapping
- SPI architecture
- Perception and control workload separation

### Embedded & IoT

**Context:** Prototyping and experimentation

Boards, indicators, displays, and connectivity explored through embedded hardware work, including the Smart Calendar concept.

- ESP32 & ESP32-S3
- WS2812B addressable LEDs
- DS3231 real-time clock
- LCD / OLED & I2C
- 74HC595 shift registers
- 74AHCT125 level shifting
- LED protection & power considerations
- Wi-Fi-connected device concepts
- Offline-first device behaviour
- Physical-button interaction
